text: Uslu dur is a total overhaul of Arma: Cold War Assault. This first video is about the light.
Malden, under occupation. The models are the originals. The light is new.
A resistance squad moves out at first light. The sun is still burning off the valley mist.
In the pine woods, morning sun falls through the haze in shafts. The guerrillas keep to cover.
On the bay, an occupier patrol boat crosses calm water that mirrors the hills and the sky.
A low winter sun lights the occupier outpost from the side. The shade stays cool and deep.
Over Everon, the clouds catch the sun, and their shadows move slowly across the hills.
Modded islands get it too. In Sinai, a camp sits under netting in the late sun.
Golden hour. Guerrillas wait at the forest edge; every tree throws a long shadow downhill.
At sunset, an occupier convoy drives into the low sun.
At dusk, the sentries at the checkpoint gather around a fire.
At night, street lamps and the fire light the occupied town. A patrol comes down the street.
Then the rain. Puddles catch the lamps, and the resistance slips past the patrol.
Out in the country, the nights are dark. A supply run drives by its headlights alone.
When a firefight breaks out, every flare, fire and shell burst lights the field.
Uslu dur. Part two covers the gameplay: Guerrilla Mode and the AI.
